transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-06
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Searchly Head of Search), Mark Taylor (CTO), Jing Wu (Senior SWE)
Shared: demo deck (https://redwood.ai/decks/search-demo), benchmark spreadsheet (link), security pack (link)

[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Liam O'Neill, our solutions engineer. How are you folks doing?
[00:06] Priya: Going good, thanks. Sorry for running a bit late, had a sync.
[00:10] Mark: All good. Curious to see how this can help our search relevance issues.
[00:15] Liam: Great, we'll keep it focused. Agenda: quick qual, then live demo of hosted embeddings + rerank, Console walkthrough, Optimize tips, Q&A, and next steps.
[00:25] Jing: Works for us.

Qualification / Context
[00:30] Maya: Priya, could you give a quick snapshot of your current stack and pain points?
[00:36] Priya: Sure. We're on a hybrid infra - search index in ElasticSearch for doc retrieval, then we do an additional neural rerank stage. Latency is a problem during peak, and our cost for candidate re-ranking at 200ms p50 is getting expensive. We currently use a mix of in-house transformers and a managed vector store (weav-- we use Weaviate for embeddings).
[00:55] Maya: Got it. And what are your SLOs for search? p95 latency, throughput?
[00:59] Priya: p95 under 500ms end-to-end for web search, and under 300ms for our internal product search. Accuracy-wise we have a labeled set and want at least a 5% lift in NDCG. Timeframe: pilot in the next 2-3 weeks.
[01:15] Mark: We'll also need to know security stuff - SOC2, SSO, audit logs, and KMS for keys.
[01:22] Liam: Totally expected, we'll cover that briefly; we can share security pack after the call.

Demo: Hosted embeddings + rerank
[01:30] Liam: I'll pull up the demo. Quick note: the hosted endpoints are two separate endpoints for this flow - the embeddings endpoint and the reranker endpoint. Our embeddings are 512/1024 vectors depending on model, and reranker returns a score + optional explanation.
[01:48] [screen share noise]
[02:00] Liam: Here in the Console, you can create an embeddings key, test with a sample doc. I'm going to show a sample flow: retrieve top-k from ElasticSearch, call Redwood embeddings for query+doc, compute dot-product or use the rerank endpoint which wraps retrieval+rerank.
[02:18] Priya: Quick question - does the rerank endpoint run on the same model as embeddings or separate model?
[02:22] Liam: Good one. It can be either. We typically use an embedding model for vector similarity and then a lightweight rerank model - sometimes the same model with cross-encoder architecture. For hosted, we offer curated combos with performance profiles.
[02:35] Jing: Are these models open models or proprietary?
[02:38] Maya: Mostly open-source models we verify and tune - we also have Redwood-verified variants. We don't expose underlying weights to customers on hosted, but it's all based on open LLM stacks.

API example & imperfect transcription
[02:45] Liam: Example request: POST /v1/embeddings with {"input": "how to reset password"} returns a vector. Then POST /v1/rerank with candidate list returns a scored list. Response has scores, tokens, and optional explainability fields. Sorry if the sample JSON here is a bit off - the console autogenerates snippets.
[03:12] [short awkward pause, typing sounds]

Performance discussion (latency vs cost)
[03:20] Mark: What's realistic p95 for rerank? If we rerank top-50, that's heavy.
[03:26] Liam: Yeah, top-50 cross-encoder rerank will be heavier. With our hosted offering, we see p95 around 150-300ms for a light reranker at top-10; top-50 pushes that higher and cost scales linearly. We recommend two patterns: 1) dense retrieval + small rerank (top-10) or 2) multi-stage: coarse embed similarity to top-200, cheap filter, then rerank top-10.
[03:50] Priya: Our current cost calc assumed re-ranking 100 candidates. Can you help us model cost?
[03:55] Maya: Yes - we'll send a cost model. For hosted it's per-embedding + per-rerank call. Liam will share the benchmark spreadsheet where you can plug in your candidate sizes and QPS.

Console: tracing & Optimize
[04:05] Liam: Console has per-route latency and token breakdown, plus traces. Here's an example trace where you can see KV cache hits and the batching efficiency. Side note: sometimes the auto transcript says K V cache, it's actually KV cache.
[04:20] Priya: Batching - can we control batch sizes or is it automatic?
[04:24] Liam: It's workload-aware automatic batching. But you can set soft targets in your project settings and Optimize will recommend config changes (batching window, max batch size) to hit latency/cost targets.
[04:35] Jing: Do you support prefix caching for repeated queries? We have lots of repeated navigational queries.
[04:39] Liam: Yes, prefix/KV caching is supported and we can pin certain prefixes; that reduces per-token compute.

Security & compliance
[04:47] Mark: Ok, security. SOC 2, SSO, KMS, data residency - hosted can we do region restriction?
[04:53] Maya: Hosted supports region selection (US/EU) for data locality. For enterprise needs we have Dedicated or Private for stricter isolation. SOC2 report and pen test summary are in the security pack; we also support SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC, audit logs, and customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for Private.
[05:10] Priya: We might need customer-managed keys if we send PII.
[05:13] Liam: For hosted we can do envelope encryption with customer KMS in some cases; for full control you'd pick Private. We'll include details in the security doc.

Objections & tradeoffs
[05:20] Mark: Concern is vendor lock-in and also observability. If we go hosted, can we migrate later to Dedicated?
[05:25] Maya: Yes, migration paths are supported; same API surface and rollout tools make it straightforward. That's one of our differentiators.
[05:32] Priya: Latency vs cost - we need to hit 300ms p95. Is that doable with hosted?
[05:36] Liam: For many workloads yes with careful config: smaller reranker, aggressive prefix caching, and Optimize tweaks. If your SLOs are tighter, Dedicated might be recommended.

Live rerank example (imperfect ASR artifacts)
[05:45] [screen share typing]
[05:50] Liam: Alright I'll run a demo query. Pulling our test dataset that approximates your doc lengths. Query: "best noise cancelling headphones" - initial retrieval from ES, now sending top-50 to rerank endpoint...
[06:10] [audio: subtle network lag]
[06:15] Liam: Results returned, top-5 reordered. You can see rerank scores and a small "why" snippet - that's the explainability module which highlights key tokens. Note: sometimes the transcript will flip product names (e.g., Redwood Optimize -> Red wood Optimize) in auto-captions.
[06:32] Priya: That reorder looks promising. How do we test it offline?
[06:36] Liam: We'll share the rerank evaluation harness. It accepts labeled queries and runs offline evals returning NDCG, MRR, and latency buckets. The benchmark spreadsheet ties that to cost.

Pilot & instrumentation
[06:48] Maya: For a pilot we'll want a small slice of traffic and a labeled holdout to measure lift. Typical pilot is 2-4 weeks. Liam will help run offline evals then a live A/B on a small percentage.
[06:58] Jing: Integration effort - do you have SDKs?
[07:02] Liam: Yes, SDKs for Node/Python and a CLI. Integration is usually a few developer days to wire retrieval -> embeddings -> rerank.

Deep dive: batching, quantization (SE speaks)
[07:15] Liam: A couple of low-level notes - we support quantized model variants for CPU inference on Dedicated, and GPU-optimized kernels for hosted. Batching windows and kernel selection are automatic but you can override in Dedicated. Also, our compilation selects op kernels depending on sequence length distribution.
[07:36] Mark: When would you recommend Dedicated vs Hosted for us?
[07:40] Liam: If your QPS is high and you need strict p95 guarantees and customer-managed keys, consider Dedicated. Hosted is faster to start and less ops overhead. Most customers prototype on hosted then move to Dedicated if needed.

Questions from Jing, minor transcript errors
[07:55] Jing: Do you keep logs for debugging? How long?
[07:58] Maya: By default 30 days, extended retention is an add-on. Audit logs are available for enterprise.
[08:05] Priya: About data deletion - can we purge data on demand?
[08:08] Liam: Yes, we provide data deletion APIs and a retention config.

Wrap-up & next steps
[08:20] Maya: Quick recap: we'll send pricing and pilot agreement, Liam will share the benchmark spreadsheet and evaluator scripts, and we'll set up a pilot kick-off next week. Any final questions?
[08:32] Mark: No, looks good. Please include cost numbers for top-10 vs top-50 rerank scenarios.
[08:36] Priya: And include SOC2 + KMS details.
[08:39] Maya: Will do. Thanks everyone.
[08:43] Jing: Thanks.

End notes: some transcription artifacts (Speaker 2 sometimes appears as "Speaker 1", auto punctuation errors), occasional filler words (uh, um) removed in places for readability but many remain to keep transcript feel.
